## URL Shortener — Complete Technical Overview

---

### Core Concepts

**Short Code** — a 7-character random string like `hygR_gx` generated by nanoid. It's the identity of every shortened URL. Every redirect, every click tracked, every cache lookup uses this as the key.

**Short URL** — the full clickable link: `http://localhost:8080/hygR_gx`. The short code is just the path segment.

**Original URL** — the long URL the user submitted: `https://example.com/very/long/path/to/something`

**Soft Delete** — instead of removing a URL from the database, we set `is_active = false`. The record stays forever — useful for analytics history and audit trails.

**Cache-Aside Pattern** — before hitting Postgres, always check Redis first. If Redis has it (cache hit), return instantly. If not (cache miss), query Postgres, then write the result back to Redis for next time.

**TTL (Time to Live)** — optional expiry on a short URL. After this time, the redirect returns `410 Gone` instead of `301`.

---

### Data Flow — What Happens on Each Request

**`POST /shorten` — creating a short URL:**

```
User submits form or JSON
        ↓
RateLimiter — blocks if IP exceeded limit
        ↓
Handler — binds and validates input
        ↓
Service.Shorten()
  ├── Check Postgres: does this URL already exist?
  │     YES → return existing short code (no duplicates)
  │     NO  → continue
  ├── Custom code provided? use it. Otherwise generate 7-char nanoid
  ├── Build URL struct (ShortCode, OriginalURL, CreatedAt, IsActive=true)
  ├── TTL provided? calculate ExpiresAt = now + ttl
  ├── Save to Postgres (source of truth)
  └── Write to Redis cache (non-fatal if fails)
        ↓
Handler returns short URL to browser (HTML) or JSON (API)
```

**`GET /:code` — the redirect:**

```
User visits http://localhost:8080/hygR_gx
        ↓
RateLimiter — blocks abuse
        ↓
Metrics middleware
  └── Captures: shortCode, IP, Referrer, UserAgent, ClickedAt
        ↓
Handler.Redirect()
        ↓
Service.Resolve()
  ├── Check Redis first (cache hit → return instantly, no DB)
  ├── Cache miss → query Postgres
  ├── Found in Postgres → write back to Redis (for next request)
  ├── Not found → ErrURLNotFound → 404
  ├── ExpiresAt in the past → ErrURLExpired → 410
  └── IsActive = false → ErrURLInactive → 410
        ↓
Handler issues 301 Moved Permanently → browser follows to original URL
        ↓
Metrics middleware (resumes after c.Next() returns)
  └── Status was 301? → SaveClick to Postgres clicks table
```

**`GET /:code/stats` — analytics:**

```
Handler extracts short code
        ↓
Repository.GetAnalytics()
  ├── COUNT(*) from clicks table → total clicks
  └── GROUP BY DATE(clicked_at) → daily breakdown (last 30 days)
        ↓
Returns AnalyticsAggregate JSON
```

---

### Architecture — Layer by Layer

```
┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│         Browser / API           │
└────────────┬────────────────────┘
             │ HTTP
┌────────────▼────────────────────┐
│         routes/routes.go        │  ← registers all routes + middleware
└────────────┬────────────────────┘
             │
┌────────────▼────────────────────┐
│         middleware/             │
│  RateLimiter → all routes       │  ← token bucket per IP, in-memory map
│  Metrics     → /:code only      │  ← runs before AND after handler
└────────────┬────────────────────┘
             │
┌────────────▼────────────────────┐
│         handler/                │
│  Home · Shorten · Redirect      │  ← HTTP in, HTTP out
│  Analytics · Health             │  ← binds request, calls service
└────────────┬────────────────────┘
             │ calls
┌────────────▼────────────────────┐
│         service/                │
│  ShortenerService               │  ← ALL business logic lives here
│  Shorten · Resolve · Delete     │  ← no HTTP, no SQL, pure Go logic
└────────────┬────────────────────┘
             │ calls via interfaces
┌────────────▼────────────────────┐
│         repository/             │
│  URLStore   (interface)         │  ← contract for URL persistence
│  CacheStore (interface)         │  ← contract for cache operations
│  ClickStore (interface)         │  ← contract for click tracking
│                                 │
│  PostgresStore → implements all │  ← real SQL, source of truth
│  RedisCache    → implements     │  ← fast cache layer
│                   CacheStore    │
└────────────┬────────────────────┘
             │
┌────────────▼────────────────────┐
│  Postgres :5432   Redis :6379   │
│  urls table       url:hygR_gx   │
│  clicks table     (JSON, 24hr)  │
└─────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Why Interfaces Matter Here

The service never knows whether it's talking to Postgres, Redis, or a mock. It only knows the interface:

```go
type ShortenerService struct {
    db    repository.URLStore    // could be Postgres, SQLite, or mock
    cache repository.CacheStore  // could be Redis, memory, or mock
}
```

This is why tests work without a real database — the test injects a `mockURLStore` that satisfies the same interface. The service code never changes.

---

### Why Two Databases

|                | Redis                  | Postgres              |
| -------------- | ---------------------- | --------------------- |
| **Purpose**    | Speed                  | Truth                 |
| **Stores**     | short code → URL JSON  | All URLs, all clicks  |
| **TTL**        | 24 hours               | Forever (soft delete) |
| **On miss**    | Falls back to Postgres | —                     |
| **On failure** | Non-fatal, skip cache  | Fatal, return error   |
| **Used for**   | Redirects (hot path)   | Shortening, analytics |

The redirect path (`GET /:code`) is the most frequent operation — millions of hits on popular links. Redis handles this in microseconds without touching Postgres. Postgres only serves as the fallback and for analytics queries.

---

### Why `c.Next()` in Metrics Middleware

```go
func Metrics(store) gin.HandlerFunc {
    return func(c *gin.Context) {
        // 1. capture request data BEFORE handler runs
        event := buildClickEvent(c)

        c.Next() // 2. run the redirect handler

        // 3. check status AFTER handler has written it
        if c.Writer.Status() == 301 {
            store.SaveClick(ctx, event) // only save real clicks
        }
    }
}
```

This pattern ensures we only track successful redirects — not 404s, not expired links, not rate-limited requests. The middleware wraps the handler, not the other way around.

---

### Testing Strategy

```
Unit tests (no DB, no Redis)
  service/shortener_test.go   → mock URLStore + mock CacheStore
  middleware/metrics_test.go  → mock ClickStore
  handler/shorten_test.go     → mock ShortenerService
  handler/redirect_test.go    → mock ShortenerService

Repository tests (sqlmock — fake SQL driver)
  repository/url_repo_test.go → real SQL logic, fake DB connection
```

Each layer is tested in isolation. Mocks implement the same interfaces as real dependencies — so if an interface changes, every mock breaks and you know what to fix.
